harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured repository-supported rsnapshot backups for /srv/data, demonstrated exact rollback after destructive modifications, retained seven daily snapshots, and verified persistence through node restarts. Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Installed Alpine-compatible rsnapshot 1.5.1 and rsync 3.5.0 without upgrading the OS or kernel.
Configured /srv/snapshots with seven retained daily snapshots of /srv/data.
Enabled Alpine's daily periodic job and persistent crond service.
Captured baseline application data, modified contents and metadata, then restored the earlier snapshot exactly.
Verified live data and retained snapshots using deterministic SHA-256 manifests covering files, directories, permissions, ownership, and symlinks.
Completed the mandatory sequential restart evidence protocol for node1 and ran a successful snapshot after the final reboot.

evidence.requirement: Compatible software while preserving installed OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: Initial and final evidence shows Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts unchanged; rsnapshot 1.5.1 and rsync 3.5.0 came from the matching Alpine repository.
rsnapshot configuration is valid, uses /srv/snapshots, retains seven daily snapshots, and runs through enabled Alpine crond scheduling.

evidence.requirement: Earlier snapshot captured exact application content
evidence.summary: The source and captured snapshot manifests match exactly at SHA-256 46017a58f8b493d0835fd3fcd587e6659ef19cec0bfb6def0ccde55e4b7d9045.

evidence.requirement: Application directory was materially modified after snapshot
evidence.summary: Proof shows changed content and mode, a deleted CSV, altered symlink, and an unwanted new file; the manifest diverged from the snapshot.
Rollback restored the original hashes, permissions, ownership, symlink and readable content, removed the unwanted file, and reproduced the original manifest hash exactly.

Healthy baseline at boot ID 8600d9bf-2a65-481a-b151-9a6238db226f, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID d076cb5a-2f49-47c4-89fa-221233a2fcdb, and recovered snapshot/data operation are directly shown.

Final healthy baseline at boot ID d076cb5a-2f49-47c4-89fa-221233a2fcdb, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 76e6083e-e7fb-4566-9ebc-66418cdd2972, active crond, valid configuration, successful post-reboot snapshot, and matching live/retained data are proven.
